parsed.explanation: Severe Risk. Enforcement is documented and recent: mass arrests (99 men in August, 22 in February 2026, one at a border post while leaving), a 2026 doubling of the maximum penalty with pending 20-year exposure, and a bill that names transsexuality in its ban on promotion and support. Custody torture was documented in 2008. Mob violence is documented, including a 2023 exhumation and burning of a man outed as gay, with four suspects apprehended. Trans people are described as often facing prosecution, arrest and violence, but the trans-specific layer is thin. No gender-recognition path exists, and there is no sourced border gender-marker screening. Name change for one feminine-presenting man in 2009 is dated and is not a protection. Sexuality law is secondary, but here it is enforced, and the state tolerates mob violence. The incident list is a documented floor. No execution or organised gender-presentation sweep is documented, so this stops short of the 0.05–0.15 tier.
